items.title: IBM’s Dividend Survived the Old IBM. Can It Survive the New One?
items.summary: IBM has raised its dividend every year since 2016 without missing a beat, but the company writing those checks today barely resembles the one that started the streak. The question is whether the math still works when acquisitions, quantum bets, and mounting debt all compete for the same cash.

items.title: AI’s $10 Trillion Buildout Will Reach 3.6% of GDP. Who’s Going to Pay for It?
items.summary: Big Tech is funneling nearly $200 billion into AI infrastructure every single quarter, a share of the economy larger than the entire railroad expansion. But the balance sheets tell a more complicated story about who is actually footing the bill.

items.title: Michael Burry sends a stark warning to Big Tech stock investors
items.summary: Michael Burry just went through five balance sheets and came back with a warning nobody on Wall Street wants to hear.

items.title: How to Know When the AI Boom Is About to Go Bust
items.summary: There might not be enough paying customers to support all the data centers.  But if those circumstances should change, and the capital window narrows enough to create a funding gap for any of the world’s most important AI startups, the momentum behind the AI trade could quickly reverse.
